## Launch and authority

`CHEAP_MODEL` is the fixed `claude-sonnet-5-5` constant. A cheap request cannot supply a competing `--model` or `--fresh`; clap and daemon validation refuse the combinations. Non-Claude and known-warm seats refuse before lifecycle writes.

The selected constant is placed in `SpawnRequest.model`, with the recorded conversation as `resume`. No caller text is assembled into a `/model` command. The existing registration wait compares the requested model with the bound registered model before reporting success (`http/mod.rs:1641-1678`); this is registration evidence, not independent proof of billing or live-model behavior.

Active-process/pane safety checks, conversation-in-use checks and parent/prime authorization for assumed-dead overrides retain their existing branches (`http/revive.rs:297-446`). The option does not kill a live seat or add an authority bypass. This review does not overstate those existing branches as new per-seat security under C33.

After successful revive, the CLI resolves its acting seat and sends the same `compact` control as an ordinary compact: empty body, not FYI, not forced, with normal caller context. Therefore ordinary compact authorization and memory-turn gates remain; there is no separate privileged compaction route.

The new option is explicit. No watcher, threshold or automatic caller is added. It reuses the existing launch site and bounded registration wait.

## Notes

The live cold seat must first be stopped using existing owner-authorized lifecycle handling. If the compact half fails, the successful Sonnet revive is not rolled back: the CLI prints its receipt and the compact failure, leaving the seat on Sonnet and uncompacted. The documented plain compact retry is accurate. Returning to Opus is another explicit revive with `--model`.

The scoped docs use placeholders and product-layout paths; no private-content or credential disclosure was established. Cost claims belong to the performance verdict, not this security result.
